title: ZeroSim: Zero-Shot Analog Circuit Evaluation with Unified Transformer Embeddings
problem: Analog circuit performance evaluation requires expensive SPICE simulations. Existing neural surrogate models lack generalization to unseen topologies and design variants.
motivation: Accelerating analog circuit design requires fast, generalizable performance prediction without retraining for new topologies.
method: The system uses a transformer (a neural network) to learn how circuit components interact with each other and creates unified numerical representations (embeddings) for all components. Since it learned the fundamental rules of how components work together, it can predict performance for new circuit layouts it has never seen before—without retraining—a capability called zero-shot inference. This approach evaluates circuits 13 times faster than running expensive SPICE simulations.
key_novelty: It learns circuit component interactions using transformer embeddings and applies that knowledge to predict performance on new circuit designs without retraining.
contributions: Unified transformer embedding scheme for circuit components
limitations: Analysis limited to abstract; actual generalization scope to different circuit families and corner cases unknown.
